index.title: Get started with Artemis
index.lead: From sign-up to your agent's first payment, in Sandbox, in five minutes.

step1.title: 1. Create an account
step1.body: Sign up on the app with your email (magic link), create your organization and register a passkey: you will use it to approve spending.

step2.title: 2. Create an agent
step2.body: In Agents, create for example notion.agent. Artemis shows its token (art_test_… in Sandbox, art_live_… with a real bank) only once: copy it.

step3.title: 3. Connect the agent
step3.fastest: The fastest way: npx artemis-agents init (see CLI).
step3.server: The MCP server is at {url}, with the header Authorization: Bearer <token>. Follow the guide for your tool: Claude, ChatGPT, n8n or REST API.

step4.title: 4. The purchase cycle
step4.requestCard: Requests a card: amount in cents, currency, merchant, purpose.
step4.getCardForCheckout: Returns an ephemeral link (10 min, single use): the card is displayed by the bank, without going through Artemis.
step4.attachReceipt: Attaches a receipt to the purchase.
step4.cancelCard: Cancels the card if the purchase no longer takes place.

step5.title: 5. Go live
step5.body: Choose a plan in Billing, then connect your bank in Banks. Agents linked to that bank receive real single-use cards.

mcpClaude.title: Connect Claude
mcpClaude.lead: Claude Code, Claude Desktop and Claude connectors speak MCP over HTTP.
mcpClaude.verify: Check with claude mcp list, then ask for example: “Subscribe us to Notion for {price} with Artemis”.
mcpClaude.desktopBody: Open Settings → Developer → Edit Config and add:

mcpChatgpt.title: Connect ChatGPT
mcpChatgpt.lead: ChatGPT accepts remote MCP servers as custom connectors.
mcpChatgpt.step1: Open Settings → Connectors → Advanced and enable developer mode if your plan requires it.
mcpChatgpt.step3: Authentication: Authorization header with the value Bearer art_… (depending on the options offered by your ChatGPT workspace).
mcpChatgpt.note: The exact labels vary between ChatGPT plans; the address and header stay the same.
mcpChatgpt.openaiBody: With the Responses API or the Agents SDK, declare a remote MCP tool pointing to {url} with the same header.

cli.title: CLI, Claude skill and n8n
cli.lead: From zero to your first mandate in three minutes.
cli.commandBody: The command asks for the API URL and the agent token (created in the app, Agents page), checks access, saves the configuration in ~/.config/artemis/config.json, adds the MCP server to Claude Code if it is installed and prints the configuration for Claude Desktop and n8n. With a Sandbox token and the --demo option, it creates a first test mandate for you to approve in the app.
cli.skillBody: The artemis-payments skill teaches Claude to pay through Artemis: amount in cents, waiting for approval, opening the payment link at the right moment, receipt after the purchase, and rejecting injections. Copy the integrations/claude-skill/artemis folder from the repository into ~/.claude/skills/.
cli.n8nBody: Install the community node n8n-nodes-artemis (Settings → Community nodes). Operations: request a card, status, payment link, cancel, budget. Credentials: API URL and agent token.

n8n.title: Connect n8n
n8n.lead: Two options: the MCP Client node for an n8n AI agent, or HTTP requests for a classic workflow.
n8n.agentBody: In an AI Agent node, add the MCP Client tool: transport HTTP Streamable, URL {url}, authentication Header Auth with Authorization: Bearer art_….
n8n.workflowBody: Import the example workflow examples/n8n/artemis-request-card.json from the repository. It chains:
n8n.step2: a polling loop on GET /v1/card-requests/:id until the status is issued;
n8n.step3: POST /v1/card-requests/:id/reveal to get the card's ephemeral link (10 minutes, single use).

api.title: REST API
api.lead: For Make, your scripts and your own agents. Same token as the MCP server.
api.base: Base URL: {url}. Limit: 60 requests per minute per agent.
api.reveal: Ephemeral link to the card (10 min, single use)
api.errorsBody: Common codes: invalid_amount (the amount must be an integer in cents), over_transaction_limit, over_monthly_budget, merchant_not_allowed, quota_exceeded, card_not_ready, already_revealed, rate_limited.

rules.title: Rules and approval
rules.lead: How Artemis decides whether a request is rejected, approved automatically or submitted for your signature.
rules.orderBody: The first rule that is not met rejects the request:
rules.o2: Positive amount below the per-purchase limit (invalid_amount, over_transaction_limit).
rules.o3: Monthly budget: the month's pending, approved and paid requests + the amount (over_monthly_budget). The month follows Paris time.
rules.o4: Blocked merchant, or missing from the allowlist if there is one (merchant_blocked, merchant_not_allowed).
rules.o5: Merchant category (MCC) blocked or not allowed (mcc_blocked, mcc_not_allowed).
rules.autoBody: A request is approved without you if its amount is below the auto-approval threshold and the merchant is on the agent's allowlist. Without an allowlist, every request is submitted to you.
rules.matchBody: Names are compared ignoring case, accents, legal form and domain extension: “Notion” covers “Notion Labs, Inc.” and “notion.so”.
rules.humanBody: Owners, admins and approvers receive a notification. Approval requires a passkey. If your bank enforces its own strong customer authentication (Qonto, for example), also approve in its app.
rules.expiryBody: An unprocessed request expires after 30 minutes (configurable). An unused card is cancelled when it expires.
